sources.title: Travel to Andorra
sources.publisher: Government of Andorra, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: Andorra's Foreign Affairs Ministry publishes this current inbound-travel guidance on its official govern.ad domain. It identifies France/Spain access and the necessary Schengen entry count where a visa is required.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The Principality of Andorra does not require any type of visa.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, consolidated 30 December 2025
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex hosts the current consolidated Regulation, in force from 30 December 2025. Articles 3–4 and Annexes I–II provide the exhaustive short-stay split relevant to entry through France or Spain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of third countries listed in Annex I shall be required to be in possession of a visa.

sources.title: Directive 2004/38/EC: right of entry for Union citizens
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex publishes the EU free-movement directive. Article 5 establishes the no-entry-visa rule for Union citizens entering a Member State with a valid identity card or passport.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No entry visa or equivalent formality may be imposed on Union citizens.

sources.title: Schengen Borders Code: persons with equivalent free-movement rights
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex hosts the consolidated Schengen Borders Code. Its free-movement definition includes third-country nationals with equivalent rights under Union and Member-State agreements.
sources.supportingExcerpt: third-country nationals ... enjoy rights of free movement equivalent to those of Union citizens

sources.title: European Travel Information and Authorisation System: current status
sources.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The European Commission's Smart Borders page reports the current operational status of ETIAS, the planned electronic travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point.

sources.title: Tripartite Convention on movement and stay in Andorra of third-country nationals
sources.officialityEvidence: Spain's Official State Gazette publishes the in-force tripartite Convention, effective 1 July 2003 and automatically renewed annually unless denounced. It coordinates entry requirements for third-country nationals entering Andorra through France or Spain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Third-country nationals may not enter Andorra without a valid travel document, where appropriate containing the required visas.

sources.title: EU visa agreements with non-EU countries
sources.officialityEvidence: The Council’s current official visa-agreements register was reviewed on 3 March 2026. Its Nauru note confirms the waiver has not begun because the agreement is not concluded.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa-free regime will apply only once Nauru and EU have concluded a visa waiver agreement.

sources.title: Recommendations when traveling
sources.publisher: Government of Andorra, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: Andorra's MFA publishes current travel-document recommendations on govern.ad. It identifies the passport as the document proving identity and nationality.
sources.supportingExcerpt: El passaport és el document que acredita la identitat i la nacionalitat d’una persona.

sources.title: Andorran nationality by origin
sources.publisher: Government of Andorra, Ministry of Justice and Interior
sources.officialityEvidence: Andorra's Justice and Interior Ministry publishes the official description of nationality by origin and when an individual is Andorran.
sources.supportingExcerpt: És andorrà l’infant nascut al Principat d’Andorra, si almenys un dels pares és andorrà.

policies.title: Andorran ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: An Andorran national travelling on an Andorran ordinary passport is classified as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: This is a citizenship classification, not a foreign visitor-visa relationship. The official passport guidance identifies the passport as proof of identity and nationality, and the Government publishes the nationality-by-origin rules.
It does not define travel by a dual national presenting another passport, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free route to Andorra through Spain or France
policies.summary: Andorra issues no visitor visa. Union citizens do not need an entry visa for the Spanish or French access leg, so these ordinary passports have a visa-free visitor route to Andorra.
conditions: Andorra has no airport and is outside Schengen; access is through France or Spain. This status means no visa is needed for the access leg, not that Andorra is a Schengen Member State.
Use a valid passport or national identity card as applicable. Normal document validity, admission and route checks remain.
No Andorran eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival is established.

policies.title: Visa-exempt Schengen-access ordinary passports: visa-free route to Andorra
policies.summary: Andorra issues no visitor visa. These passports are visa-exempt for the needed Schengen access leg under Annex II or equivalent free-movement arrangements, and therefore have a visa-free route to Andorra.
conditions: Andorra is outside Schengen and has no airport; access is through France or Spain. Annex II exempts applicable third-country passports for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
Biometric passport is required for AL, BA, GE, MD, ME, MK, RS, UA and XK. Taiwan requires the identity-card number in the passport; HK and MO require their named SAR passports.
CH, IS, LI and NO follow equivalent free-movement treatment for the access leg; this does not make Andorra part of Schengen.

For non-EU minors, the Andorran guidance expressly requires a two- or multiple-entry Schengen visa. This age-specific requirement is retained and does not convert the adult Annex II ordinary-passport baseline into a visa requirement.
ETIAS is not operating on the research date. Do not normalize its planned future operation as a current ETA requirement.
No Andorran eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established. Passport validity, purpose, funds, return/onward travel and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Annex I ordinary passports: Schengen visa required to reach Andorra
policies.summary: Andorra itself issues no visitor visa, but these passports require a Schengen visa to cross the French or Spanish external border needed to reach Andorra. The Andorran Government requires a double-entry or multiple-entry Schengen visa according to planned exits and returns.
conditions: This is a Schengen advance-visa requirement for the actual France/Spain access leg, not a separate Andorran visa: Andorra requires no type of visa.

Obtain a double-entry Schengen visa for one exit from Andorra and return to Schengen; obtain a multiple-entry Schengen visa for several exits and returns. A single-entry visa does not preserve the return leg.
Apply through the competent French or Spanish consular route. A short-stay visa normally concerns up to 90 days in any 180-day period; issuance and final entry are separate.

No Andorran eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival is established. Residence permits, long-stay visas, family-member rights, diplomatic/official/service documents, local-border permits and other exceptions are not flattened into this baseline.

application.label: European Commission: applying for a Schengen visa
application.processingTime: Apply at least 15 days before travel and no earlier than six months before the journey; individual cases can take longer.
steps: Choose the French or Spanish consular route corresponding to the intended Schengen access itinerary and lodging rules.
Apply for a Schengen short-stay visa with enough double or multiple entries for every planned exit from Andorra and return to Schengen.
Receive the visa before travel and present the valid travel document, visa and supporting documents for border control.

policies.title: Nauru ordinary passport: Schengen visa required pending EU waiver agreement
policies.summary: Although Nauru appears in Annex II, its footnote makes exemption conditional on entry into force of an EU waiver agreement. The current Council register says the regime applies only once Nauru and the EU have concluded that agreement; the ordinary-passport route to Andorra therefore remains Schengen visa required.
conditions: Andorra has no separate visitor visa; this is the Schengen visa required for travel through France or Spain to reach Andorra.
The Annex II Nauru footnote is conditional. Do not classify Nauru as visa-free until an official source confirms the EU–Nauru waiver agreement is concluded and in force.
If a visa is required, use double entry for one exit from Andorra and return to Schengen, or multiple entry for several exits and returns.
